title: Proton-transfer acid-base relation
statement: Proton transfer moves one named proton carrier from one registered donor occurrence to one distinct acceptor occurrence while conserving carrier identity and both endpoint records.
generation_rule: Generate the literal product of the registered proton carrier, source, destination, transition, identity, closure, record and extension choices.
grammar_boundary: Every finite chemical transition in which one named proton carrier leaves one registered donor occurrence and enters one distinct registered acceptor occurrence with identical carrier identity before and after.

choices.name: proton-count-only
choices.reason: A count cannot establish conservation of an occurrence.

choices.name: one-named-proton-carrier
choices.reason: The transferred proton identity remains held.

choices.name: source-erased
choices.reason: Without a donor, the carrier could be created freely.

choices.name: destination-erased
choices.reason: Without an acceptor, the carrier could be lost.

choices.name: copy-or-delete
choices.reason: Copying or deleting violates carrier conservation.

choices.name: donor-to-acceptor-transfer
choices.reason: One carrier changes endpoint exactly once.

choices.name: before-after-carrier-change
choices.reason: A changed carrier is not transfer conservation.

choices.name: same-carrier-before-after
choices.reason: The proton occurrence is identical across the transition.

choices.name: unpaired-composition-change
choices.reason: Unpaired change leaves the reaction record open.

choices.name: complete-endpoint-closure
choices.reason: Donor loss and acceptor gain are one event.

choices.name: product-label-only
choices.reason: A product label cannot reconstruct the path.

choices.name: carrier-endpoint-transition-trace
choices.reason: Carrier and both endpoints remain auditable.

choices.name: free-proton-source
choices.reason: A free source can force any reaction.

choices.name: no-extra-rule
choices.reason: Conserved endpoint transfer supplies the law.

induction_base: One named proton carrier with one distinct donor and acceptor supplies the first closed transfer.
induction_step: Appending one independent transfer preserves every prior carrier and endpoint identity and closes only through paired donor loss and acceptor gain.
exclusions: no acid/base dictionary, pH scale, equilibrium equation, dissociation constant, measured value or V2 answer may select a candidate
no numerical zero, negative, irrational, imaginary or floating proof quantity
no free, fitted, learned or target-derived parameter
no unpaired creation, copying or loss of a proton or electron carrier
no claim that structural closure alone fixes every solution-dependent strength or capacity value
external target content remains inaccessible until the prediction is sealed

Every finite chemical transition in which one named proton carrier leaves one registered donor occurrence and enters one distinct registered acceptor occurrence with identical carrier identity before and after.
operational_witnesses: the transfer retains one proton occurrence
donor and acceptor occurrences are distinct
one event has one retained carrier

target_rows.source_locator: official IUPAC source set anchored at P04915

falsification_condition: The claim fails if the authoritative proton-transfer record lacks a proton donor, proton acceptor or conserved transfer relation, or if a changed row is accepted.
